response.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS matched_order_count
  FROM riskandmargin AS r
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.recordvault = r.ordervault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
), average_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(matched_order_count) AS avg_count
  FROM counts
)
SELECT a.avg_count AS average_count,
       AVG(c.matched_order_count - a.avg_count) AS average_excess
FROM counts AS c
CROSS JOIN average_count AS a
WHERE c.matched_order_count > a.avg_count;

assumptions.assumption: Counts each matching risk/margin record as one matched order; if an order has multiple matching risk/margin records, it contributes multiple times.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct orders per order type, so multiple risk/margin records matching the same order contribute only once.
alternatives.sql:
WITH counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS matched_order_count
  FROM riskandmargin AS r
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.recordvault = r.ordervault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
), average_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(matched_order_count) AS avg_count
  FROM counts
)
SELECT a.avg_count AS average_count,
       AVG(c.matched_order_count - a.avg_count) AS average_excess
FROM counts AS c
CROSS JOIN average_count AS a
WHERE c.matched_order_count > a.avg_count;
